newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: COLOMBIAN REBELS BLAST TWO MINOR PIPELINES.
newsitem.headline: COLOMBIAN REBELS BLAST TWO MINOR PIPELINES.

text.p: Leftist rebels dynamited two minor pipelines of no strategic importance early Tuesday, a spokesman for the state-run oil company Ecopetrol said.
The first attack was on a 12-inch line that pumps crude from the El Centro field, one of Colombia's oldest, to the oil production center of Barrancabermeja in northern Santander province.
The pipeline was not pumping at the time and only a small amount of oil was spilled, the Ecopetrol spokesman said. The blast was blamed on the National Liberation Army (ELN).

The second explosion, blamed on the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), occurred in southern Putumayo province and ruptured a six-inch pipeline operated by U.S. oil company Argosy Energy International.
Putumayo produces only about 10,000 barrels of crude per day which is pumped to the pacific coast port of Tumaco.
"Neither of these pipelines had any strategic significance," the Ecopetrol spokesman said.

The ELN, set up by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966, specializes in attacks on key oil infrastructure and has frequently paralyzed pumping along the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline, the second largest in the country.
